Scientific questions, small models, and the evidence behind predictions. A practical course for master's students in chemistry, taught by Kevin Maik Jablonka.

## Next class: 11 November

**12:10–16:00.** We start with our first Python notebook, then work through a machine-learning lecture on training, kernels, standardisation, and testing. The MOF notebook is available throughout, with time to work together in class and continue on 2 December. Bring your laptop, charger, and any setup questions.

## How we work {#how-to-use-a-lecture-page}

Explanations and handwritten examples lead into calculations you can inspect, change, and discuss. Unfinished attempts are welcome. Collect project ideas in the shared document linked in the course email. The [assessment](outline.qmd#assessment) combines a project report and a presentation with discussion; submission dates will be announced on the course outline page and by email.

[]{#feedback}

Tell me what helped you understand something and what got in the way. Your feedback helps me adjust the next session.
